title: Add intent-aware notification filters and sampling policy
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: On-call teams have a high volume of low-signal alert noise (e.g., repeated retries, background job churn) that reduces attention for real regressions. This PR introduces an intent-aware notification filter subsystem in slo-toolkit to reduce pager noise by classifying alert intent and applying a configurable sampling policy. Design: intent-classifier is a small inference pipeline (lightweight TF/onnx model) that tags alert events with intent labels (user-impact, background, transient, informational). A configurable rule engine maps intents + alert metadata (service, severity, recent-alert-rate) to a delivery decision: deliver, hold-and-sample, or suppress-with-explanation. The subsystem exposes a simple SDK hook that incident-bot and other consumers can call synchronously before creating an incident or sending a page. Backwards compatibility: default policy is passthrough (no suppression). Admins can opt-in per-service via slo-toolkit config. Rollout plan: staged canary in three services, 7-day ramp with metrics guarded alert-volume, pager-rate, and missed-severity-1s. Implementation notes: added a classifier wrapper, rule engine, CLI tools to preview how a rule would behave against a window of historical alerts, and a small bridge in the incident-bot integration to annotate suppressed alerts with reasoning. Testing: unit tests for rule resolution, integration test with a small synthetic alert generator, load test to ensure classifier adds <5ms p50 latency. Security & privacy: classifier runs on alert metadata only (no full trace payloads) and respects KMS keys for model artifacts. See linked Linear items for evaluation dataset and model-retraining plan.

review_conversation: Samir: asked for metrics to guard rollout (added alert-volume, oncall-pager-rate, missed-p0) and requested a non-blocking opt-in; addressed by making default passthrough and adding per-service enable flag. Elena: requested more explicit reasoning in incident logs for suppressed alerts; added structured annotation and example log format. Jordan: flagged potential latency regressions; added microbenchmark results and moved model loading to warm-start path. Author responses: implemented requested telemetry, added CLI preview, and trimmed runtime allocations. Final: reviewers approved after CI green and a short canary run in staging.
merge_outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-18. Commit message summarizes feature, rollout, and safeguards. Release notes added below.
release_notes: Add intent-aware notification filtering with opt-in per-service configuration.
New CLI command `sloctl preview-filter` to simulate filter outcomes against historical windows.
Default behaviour remains passthrough; no suppression occurs unless enabled.
